directive:
D-orchestrator directive for angle 0 revision v2. The reviewer returned REVISE at tier=field with BOTH theorems judged NEW on both axes. The kernel is accepted: do NOT change the research question, the two theorem targets, or the OEQ. Fix exactly the three defects below and resubmit.

(1) WELL-POSEDNESS OF THE CLASS (soundness flag C-wellposed, load-bearing — must fix).
The class currently overloads a single constant M as (i) the outcome envelope |Y| <= M, (ii) the Hoelder radius for all four smoothness assumptions, and (iii) the covariate-density envelope p_X <= M. Since p_X is a probability density on [0,1]^d, p_X <= M forces M >= 1, so the class is EMPTY for M < 1 and the minimax functional and every positive lower bound are undefined on part of the declared parameter domain. Repair by SEPARATING the envelope constants rather than by patching a single inequality: use an outcome bound M_Y > 0 in ass:bounded-outcome and def:estimator-class, a Hoelder radius L > 0 shared by ass:mu-a-holder / ass:pi-a-holder / ass:mu-x-holder / ass:pi-x-holder, and a covariate-density envelope pbar >= 1 in ass:px-bounded. Update def:holder-class, def:minimax-mse, def:estimator-class, both theorem statements and the OEQ statement so every occurrence of M is replaced by the correct one of M_Y / L / pbar, and update free_symbols and the symbols table accordingly. Then ADD an explicit nonemptiness statement to the proposal: exhibit a concrete witness law in P(alpha,beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0) for every admissible parameter tuple (e.g. X uniform on [0,1]^d, pi(a|x) uniform on [0,1], mu identically zero, Y = 0), so the class is certified nonempty and the sup in def:minimax-mse is over a nonempty index set. State the admissible parameter domain explicitly (M_Y > 0, L > 0, pbar >= 1, 0 < c <= 1, t_0 in the interior of [0,1], alpha, beta, s > 0, d >= 1). All constants remain n-free, so this repair changes no exponent and no theorem content.

(2) CITATION MISCHARACTERIZATION (novelty flag N-mischar — must fix).
BalakrishnanKennedyWasserman2023 (arXiv:2305.04116) is titled "The Fundamental Limits of Structure-Agnostic Functional Estimation" and is a general black-box nuisance / functional-estimation minimax lower-bound paper; causal inference is motivation, not its title or its exclusive scope. Correct the title and the scope description in BOTH the bibliography entry and the related_work commentary, and re-state the differentiation on the correct ground: it gives structure-agnostic lower bounds that do not bind inside a Hoelder smoothness model, hence it neither implies nor contradicts a beta-invariance claim in this class.
Also ADD Schindl, Shen and Kennedy (2024) on minimax rates for incremental / continuous-exposure effects as a nearby continuous-exposure minimax comparator, with commentary that distinguishes its incremental (shift / edge-of-support) target from the FIXED INTERIOR dose t_0 partial mean studied here, and note that an incremental target does not localize in the treatment coordinate and therefore carries no alpha-vs-beta elbow of the kind at issue. Verify the exact title, venue and year before citing; if you cannot verify it, cite it with the verified metadata you can confirm and say so in the commentary rather than inventing a locator.

(3) MATCHED-ASSUMPTION BOUNDARY FOR THE STRICT-TIGHTENING CLAIM (must fix — this is what makes the headline checkable).
The claim that thm:oracle-high-s is strictly faster than Bonvini-Kennedy Theorem 3.1 is only meaningful against a stated assumption boundary. Add to the proposal a theorem-side comparison table with one row per compared result and columns: (a) the exact class / assumptions assumed, (b) the extra conditional ingredients the comparator requires beyond the bare class declared here -- for Bonvini-Kennedy's oracle branch name them explicitly (specified HOIF estimator of a given order, projection-kernel / basis choice, and the density-estimation remainder assumed negligible), (c) the risk notion (conditional-on-nuisance-sample risk vs unconditional minimax MSE over the class), and (d) the resulting exponent. Make explicit that Bonvini-Kennedy Theorem 3.1 is an UPPER bound for one specified estimator under a conditional risk, not a minimax statement, so this proposal's contribution is a same-class minimax comparison and not a contradiction of their theorem. Keep the comparator_promise_table consistent with this new table.

Additionally, keep the OEQ oeq:deficient-frontier honestly positioned: the repo-axis call on it was "incremental" relative to the banked stat_dose_response_minimax / holder_anisotropic_converse frontier OEQ, so word it explicitly as a sharper successor to that preserved handle (same class, now asking for the exact beta-free exponent in the deficient covariate regime), not as a fresh open question.

Do not add any assumption that encodes the crux (in particular, do not assume beta-freeness, do not assume the HOIF remainder is negligible, and do not add extra covariate-density smoothness) in order to make the targets easier. Keep tldr, project_justification and related_work in step with any wording that changes.

D-orchestrator directive for angle 0 revision v4. The v3 review cleared ALL soundness flags (C=0) and again judged both theorems NEW on both axes at tier=field. The math kernel is accepted and settled: do NOT change the research question, the definitions, the two theorem targets, or the OEQ. Exactly one defect class remains, and it has now recurred three rounds running on three different citations (BKW in v1, Schindl in v2, the two Kim--Wang entries in v3). That means the symptom has been patched each round while the ROOT was never fixed. The root is that bibliography entries -- several inherited verbatim from the topic anchor -- were carried into the draft without being checked against their actual sources. Fix the ROOT this round.

(A) THE TWO FALSE ENTRIES, WITH THE VERIFIED RECORDS.
The reviewer verified both from source. Use these records exactly.

  (A1) arXiv:2510.19094 is NOT a Kim--Wang paper. It is "Estimation of causal dose-response functions under data fusion" by Jaewon Lim and Alex Luedtke (arXiv:2510.19094v1, 21 October 2025), which studies a data-fusion orthogonal-loss framework. Delete the bibkey KimWang2025 entirely, replace it with a correctly attributed LimLuedtke2025 entry, and rewrite its related_work and comparator-table commentary on the correct ground: it is a data-fusion dose-response estimation framework, so it neither targets nor bounds the single-population fixed-dose minimax MSE at issue here, and its class carries no treatment-density smoothness coordinate. Remove any claim that it contains an "integrated-risk RKHS/Sobolev lower bound" -- that characterization came from the topic anchor and is false of this paper.

  (A2) arXiv:2604.13410 IS a real, accessible Kim--Wang paper: "Estimating Continuous Treatment Effects with Two-Stage Kernel Ridge Regression" by Seok-Jin Kim and Kaizheng Wang (arXiv:2604.13410v2, 28 May 2026), which targets MISE, gives a DENSITY-FREE two-stage KRR upper bound, and states a matching Sobolev MISE lower bound (objective (2.1); Theorems 4.1 and 4.3). The v3 draft described its title and venue as externally unverifiable; that is wrong and it suppressed a genuinely close comparator. Cite it correctly with that locator and treat it as a CLOSE but non-subsuming comparator -- do not hide it, and do not overstate it.

(B) THE KIM--WANG COMPARISON, DONE PROPERLY (this is the substantive part).
Because Kim--Wang is density-free and has matching MISE bounds, it is the nearest thing in the literature to a beta-free statement, so the proposal must say precisely why it neither supplies nor rules out the proposed pointwise beta-invariance theorem. Add a theorem-side comparison row/table for it with these axes, each answered explicitly:
  (a) RISK GEOMETRY -- their target is MISE, an integrated risk over the dose interval; the proposal's target is pointwise MSE at a fixed interior dose t_0. An integrated-risk rate neither implies nor is implied by a pointwise rate at a fixed point, and integration can average away exactly the local dose-localization difficulty that the alpha-vs-beta elbow is about.
  (b) FUNCTION CLASS -- their class is RKHS/Sobolev; the proposal's is anisotropic Hoelder with SEPARATE exponents alpha (dose), beta (treatment density) and s (covariates). State plainly that their class contains NO treatment-density smoothness index at all, so no result stated over it can answer whether the minimax exponent depends on beta: the question is not expressible in their model.
  (c) OVERLAP / DESIGN CONDITIONS -- state what their result assumes about the treatment design and how it compares to the proposal's two-sided positivity c <= pi(a|x) <= 1/c.
  (d) WHETHER THEIR DENSITY-FREENESS ALREADY GIVES THE CLAIM -- answer this head-on rather than leaving it implicit: their bound being density-free is an absence of a beta index in their class, not a proof that beta is irrelevant in a class where beta IS an index; a density-free MISE rate over a Sobolev class is consistent with beta-sensitivity of the pointwise Hoelder-class minimax rate, so their theorem does not settle the question in either direction. If any remark in their paper (e.g. an L-infinity or sup-norm remark) could be read as yielding a pointwise rate, address that remark specifically and say why it does or does not transfer to this class.

(C) ROOT FIX -- VERIFY EVERY REMAINING BIBLIOGRAPHY ENTRY THIS ROUND, NOT JUST THE FLAGGED ONES.
Before resubmitting, go through the bibliography ENTRY BY ENTRY -- every one, including the ones no reviewer has flagged and every one inherited from the topic anchor -- and confirm against the actual source (use the arXiv HTML / LaTeX rendering or the publisher record; PDFs are unreliable) all four of: exact title, author list, venue and year, and the specific claim the draft attributes to it together with a concrete locator (theorem/section/page). Then, for each entry, do ONE of:
  - keep it, with the verified metadata and locator recorded;
  - correct it to the verified record and rewrite the commentary that depended on the wrong record;
  - or delete it, if you cannot verify it against a source this round.
Never carry a characterization you have not verified, and never describe a verifiable paper as unverifiable. A weaker claim that you have checked always beats a stronger claim that you have not. Record in the iteration trail that this full sweep was performed, so this defect class does not return.

(D) UNCHANGED STANDING INSTRUCTIONS. Keep blocking the reviewer's high-effort strengthening path: do NOT pre-specify the beta-free estimator (localized moment, projection family, normalization, tuning schedule). The estimator and every mechanic inside it are deliberately NOT pre-committed in this run; constructing them is the Stage 0 derivation work, and the iteration trail already records that decision -- keep that note. Add no assumption that encodes the crux (no assumed beta-freeness, no assumed negligible HOIF or density-estimation remainder, no extra covariate-density smoothness). Keep the v2/v3 well-posedness repairs (designated jointly measurable Hoelder versions, the finite-beta convention, the nonemptiness witness) exactly as they now stand -- they passed. Keep tldr, project_justification, related_work and comparator_promise_table in step with every change above.
